tags.notes: Garden Eel Cove (Makako Bay) — primary Kona manta site. Sandy bottom at ~9m. Reef manta (Mobula alfredi). Widely reported 450+ catalogued resident rays (konahonudivers.com); 80-90% sighting success rate year-round. Corrected origin story: hotel floodlights at Kona Surf Hotel began attracting mantas in the early 1970s; commercial night-dive tours (Kona Coast Divers) began in 1991 — the site did not 'open' in 1991, tours started then.

Marine Life Conservation District established 1969 (confirmed by DLNR), 315 acres. Ka'awaloa Cove near Cook Monument. Depth 5-120ft/1.5-36m (DLNR confirmed). Spinner dolphins documented, arriving after dawn and resting through midday; NOAA federal rule (since 2021) prohibits approach within 50 yards. Fish species count DISPUTED across sources (100+ to 200+); no single authoritative count found — DLNR does not publish a specific number. Access rule corrected: 2013 State Parks changes restricted unpermitted kayak launching/landing at Ka'awaloa Flat and require a permit for all vessels (motorized vessels operate no-wake); this is not a full motorized-boat ban — licensed charter operators access under permit, not exclusively non-motorised craft.

Shore dive at Crescent Beach (Alua/Dog Beach/Nai'a Bay). Depth 0-27m (90ft). Tiger sharks (Galeocerdo cuvier) are documented residents, most commonly cited as one of the most reliable places in the world to encounter them; moray eels, octopus, colorful reef fish. Active boat channel — intermediate navigation required. Known by multiple names: Manta Ray Bay, Nai'a Bay, Crescent Beach, Alua Beach. Re-audit note: the specific 'over 20 tiger sharks' population figure could not be re-confirmed against 2+ independent sources this pass and has been removed as an unverified specific number; qualitative 'well-documented resident population' retained instead.

Also called Manta Ray Heaven / Makako Bay. Hawaiian garden eels (Gorgasia hawaiiensis) in sand at ~24m (80ft). Campfire/night-dive viewing area at ~10m (35ft). Kona Honu Divers exclusively uses this site since 2018. Protected from south swell by Keahole Point. Site established for manta viewing in August 1999 by James Wing (Eco-Adventures) — re-confirmed this pass via mantarayadvocates.com: 6 mantas appeared the first night including individuals later named Lefty and Big Bertha; James Wing also built the 'campfire' stone ring still used today.

Lava tube/cavern system on North Kona Coast. Surge-dependent dive. Standard morning two-tank site, commonly paired with Pyramid Pinnacle and/or Skull Rock/Skull Cave (re-confirmed this pass). Spiny lobsters, porcupine pufferfish, octopus documented by multiple operator/forum sources. Other sources reference turtles/white-tip sharks at this general site pairing but not confirmed specific to Suck Em Up itself — not added.

Series of lava fingers with arches, tubes, caves. Reef top ~3m, drops to ~18m, then deeper. Hawaiian green sea turtle (Chelonia mydas) cleaning station confirmed. White-tip reef sharks in pukas (caves). Spotted eagle rays documented. Large ulua (trevally, 200+ lb reported) confirmed by greatestdivesites.com. Multiple entry points along Puako Beach Drive. Difficulty upgraded to Intermediate: wind-driven surface chop, navigation over long shallow reef, active boat traffic concern. Re-audit: confirmed hawaii.greatestdivesites.com/hawaii_big_island/puako is genuinely Puako-specific content (verified directly this pass).

Umbrella entry covering Black Point, Frog Rock, Lava Dome (primary sites). Frog Rock: ~6-21m (20-70ft), lava tubes with interconnecting caverns, porcupine puffers, octopus, strong currents possible. Lava Dome: ~9-27m (30-90ft), dome ~9m/30ft high with centuries-old coral head, 'Pink Floyd' ledge with schooling fish. Black Point: new this pass — lovebigisland.com confirms Black Point is known for encounters with large lobsters (single-source, not yet cross-confirmed). Marine life confirmed: white-mouth moray eels, leaf scorpionfish, frogfish, arc-eye hawkfish, snowball nudibranch, marbled shrimp, blue dragon nudibranch, red soldierfish. site_type updated to cave (lava tube/cavern primary character).

South Kona near Miloli'i, also called Tubastrea Tunnel by some sources (dive-the-world.com). Lava tube ~40ft (13m) long decorated with Tubastrea coral; max site depth re-confirmed this pass at ~40ft/13m (dive-the-world.com), consistent with existing 12m depth field. Resident frogfish (3 reported). Green turtles documented. Far from shore — primarily liveaboard or long-range boat access. Water temp slightly cooler than Kona average (~24°C/75°F).

North Kona coast. Sources disagree on depth of pinnacle top to surface: 25ft/~7.6m per one source, 15ft/~4.6m per another (liveaboard.com) — reported as a range rather than a single figure. Max depth ~18m (12m average) confirmed by multiple sources. Natural cleaning station for Hawaiian green sea turtles (Chelonia mydas). Cleaner fish: surgeonfish/tang (family Acanthuridae), re-confirmed this pass. Visibility 45-60m. Light currents typical. Suitable all cert levels.

Miloli'i Bay area. Collapsed lava tube grottoes with skylights. Max depth ~12m (40ft), re-confirmed via underwaterjournal.com. Fish life described by multiple independent sources as 'average'/underwhelming — name is considered misleading by divers; a Zentacle reviewer rated Miloli'i Bay itself far superior. Re-audit CORRECTION: the two prior validation_source domains (konasnorkelandsail.com, hawaii.greatestdivesites.com) do not actually contain Aquarium-specific content — greatestdivesites.com's Puako URL was miscited here (it is a real source, but for the Puako Reef site, not this one) and konasnorkelandsail.com has no Aquarium-specific content found. Both replaced with verified sources. The prior claim that green turtles are 'confirmed abundant' at this specific site was not supported by a site-specific source (only general Kona-coast turtle abundance) and has been corrected to avoid overstating site-specific turtle confirmation.
